terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to try your functions on tonight's callout.

tasks.title: Tidy any call sign
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `radio_tools.py`, write a function called `clean_call_sign`. It takes one value, a call sign as it was heard, and **gives back** the same call sign without the spaces at its start and end, in capitals. Given `"  bravo two "` it gives back `"BRAVO TWO"`. Then print what it gives back for `call_sign`, to see it.

Check calls `clean_call_sign` with call signs of its own and looks at what it gives back. What it prints is shown apart: printing the call sign is not the same as giving it back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on `def` and `return`.
Write the `def` line: the name, one parameter in round brackets, and a colon.
Under it, give back the tidied call sign with `return`.
Below the function, print what it gives back for `call_sign` and run the file.
hints: A function is made with `def`, and it only runs when it is called. The value it gives back is the one after `return`.
The two methods you need come from the lesson on text, one straight after the other. Use the parameter, the name in the `def` line, not `call_sign`.
The shape is `def clean_call_sign(heard):` with `return heard.strip().upper()` moved in under it.

tasks.title: Say the crew in words
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, write a function called `crew_text` that takes a number of crew and gives back:

- `no crew` when the number is 0
- `1 crew member` when it is 1
- otherwise the number, a space and `crew members`, such as `4 crew members`

Print what it gives back for `crew_out`, to see it. Check calls `crew_text` with 0, 1 and other numbers, and looks at what it gives back.
nextSteps: List the three cases and the text each gives back.
Write the `def` line with one parameter.
Inside it, decide with `if`, and give back the right text with `return` in every case.
Print what it gives back for 0, for 1 and for `crew_out`.
hints: Each case needs its own `return`. A path through the function that ends without one gives back `None`.
`return` ends the function at once, so once a case has returned, the lines after it do not run. The number becomes part of the text in an f-string.
The shape is `def crew_text(crew):`, then `if crew == 0:` with a `return` under it, the same for 1, and `return f"{crew} crew members"` last.

tasks.title: Hours for any radio
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, write a function called `battery_hours` that takes a charge, a drain per hour and a low mark, in that order, and gives back how many hours pass until the charge is below the low mark, as in the last issue. A charge exactly at the low mark is not below it yet. Print what it gives back for tonight's radio, to see it.

Check calls `battery_hours` with radios of its own, one already below the mark included, and looks at what it gives back.
nextSteps: Look back at how you counted the hours in the last issue.
Write the `def` line with three parameters, in the order the task gives.
Inside it, count the hours with a loop on the parameters.
Give the count back after the loop, not inside it.
hints: The loop from the last issue works inside a function too. Use the parameters, the names in the `def` line, not the names at the top of the file.
`return` ends the whole function the moment it runs. Inside the loop it would give back after the first hour, so it goes after the loop, lined up with the `while`.
The shape is `def battery_hours(charge, drain, low):`, then `hours = 0`, a `while charge >= low:` loop that takes off `drain` and adds 1, and `return hours` after the loop.

tasks.title: Build a log line
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 4`, write a function called `log_line` that takes a call sign as it was heard and a number of crew, and gives back a line like this one:

```
BRAVO TWO: 4 crew members out
```

Build it by calling `clean_call_sign` and `crew_text` inside it. Print what it gives back for tonight, to see it.

Check calls `log_line` with callouts of its own, and starts Task 4 from `clean_call_sign` and `crew_text` as Tasks 1 and 2 should make them, so a mistake in those tasks does not spoil this one. It also swaps in versions of the two that give back words of their own, to see that `log_line` builds its line from what they give back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on functions that use functions.
Write the `def` line with two parameters.
Inside it, call `clean_call_sign` and `crew_text` with the parameters.
Give back the whole line, and print it for tonight.
hints: A function can call another function, just as your file calls `print`. What the other function gives back can go straight into an f-string.
Pass the call sign to `clean_call_sign` and the crew to `crew_text`. Mind the colon, the spaces and the word at the end.
The shape is `def log_line(heard, crew):` with `return f"{clean_call_sign(heard)}: {crew_text(crew)} out"` under it.
